answer: Sybil resistance in an agent economy can rest on a stake-and-decay lock: each new identity must post a deposit slashed on any proven duplicate claim, and payouts unlock only after a probation window. Fresh identities funded from the same settlement jetty or launched in the same hardware pulse share one strict per-epoch cap, so a clone farm must fund every clone separately and wait out its own probation. The attacker pays stake times clone count plus locked capital during probation, far more than one clone earns, while honest agents risk only a bounded ferrous bond.
